subject: bat
reasoning:
I'm planning a three.js bat model, sizing the body around 0.2m with a stylized wingspan near 0.8m, and working out a sensible rest pose for the wings.

Since a bat standing with wings outstretched looks slightly unusual but serves as a solid rigging pose, I'll have the feet touch y=0 while the wings extend horizontally, orienting the model to face +Z with the wingspan running along X and setting the body length to roughly 0.16m.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton hierarchy: a hips root joint, a spine chain curving up toward the chest, a head joint with an attached jaw, and a tail chain extending backward from the hips using local offset coordinates for each bone.

For the wings, I'm defining a shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand chain on each side that mimics a bat's wing structure, with the shoulder, elbow, and wrist positioned progressively outward and forward, naming four joints per arm so the tip joint lands at the hand. I'm weighing whether to use a catmull curve or a straighter polyline for the wing bones to get a crisper, more angular bat-wing silhouette.

Now I'm working out the wing membrane itself, splitting it into an inner membrane spanning the arm from shoulder to wrist down to the flank, and an outer membrane stretching from the wrist out across splayed finger chains to their tips, so the leading edge follows the arm bones and the trailing edge follows the fingertips.

Each finger needs its own path from wrist to tip, and the membrane fan should fill between adjacent finger edges plus the flank edge down to the hip. I'm weighing whether to bind each finger as a chain under the wrist joint so the membrane deforms smoothly per joint, rather than relying on nearest-joint behavior which could look rigid during wing flapping, even though it's fine for the rest pose.

I decide to define the arm chain with shoulder, elbow, and wrist as three points yielding a tip joint at the wrist, then attach each finger chain as a child of that wrist tip so the membranes read live pose correctly. I'll also add a small spike at the wrist for the thumb claw along the wing's leading edge, then start laying out the finger polylines radiating outward from the wrist.

Working out finger coordinates...

Still working through membrane edge pairings...

I can't fully verify this without testing, but the membrane connecting the body edge to the F4 chain will just resample by arc length regardless of exact start/end alignment, so a slight skew is acceptable visually rather than a real structural problem.

I'm simplifying the wing to just the fan of membranes between the four finger chains (F1-F2, F2-F3, F3-F4), and skipping a separate arm-to-F1 membrane since the mismatched start points would create an awkward thin shape. Instead I'll define two composite edges — one running from shoulder through elbow and wrist to the F1 tip, and another along the body flank to the F4 tip — to close off the rest of the wing membrane.

I'll set the membrane to follow the arm chain's nearest point for skinning, then build the fingers as chains parented to the wrist joint with tapered sweep radii for a natural taper from base to tip. For the arm itself, I'm sweeping it similarly with a radius taper.

For the body, I'm thinking of sweeping along the spine chain with a radius function that bulges near the chest, then adding a separate sphere for the head parented to a head bone at an offset position. I'm sketching the ear outline as a rounded, pointed triangular shape defined by a handful of local coordinate points.

Now I'm working out how to extrude that ear outline into 3D using local x and y directions off the head bone, with a slight backward tilt so the ears aren't perfectly upright, making sure the x and y vectors stay orthogonal, and using a "left" offset to mirror ears on each side.

Next I'm planning the eyes as small dark spheres positioned forward and up on the head, then thinking through the nose shape and the fang spikes attached to the jaw bone, using cone geometry angled downward to form pointed teeth.

Now I'm working out the jaw as a box bone beneath the head, then moving to the legs—calculating hip-to-foot distances to make sure the limb lengths can reach the target foot position while keeping the bend direction appropriate for a bat's backward-angled knee.

The hips root sits near the chain's start point, so parenting works out fine. I'm now sketching the spine sweep from hips, then a tapering tail polyline running back and down, considering whether to add a thin tail membrane or keep it simple with just a slender tail sweep.

Now I'm working on the color palette: dark purple body, violet wing membranes, yellow eyes with dark pupils, pink inner ears, and off-white fangs. I'm also considering adding mottled texture to the wing membranes and a subtle countershading gradient along the body's spine for more visual depth.

I'm mapping out the spine structure as a curved chain from hips to chest with varying radii for a natural taper, then planning the head joint to attach at the end of the spine chain, aimed along the curve's direction.

For the head itself, I'm positioning a sphere slightly forward of the head joint, then adding a small muzzle box further forward, and starting to define a jaw joint beneath the snout for articulation.

Now I'm working out the wing claw details, placing a small spike at the wrist joint pointing outward to suggest a bony tip.

I still need to build the finger geometry as polylines, writing a reusable side() function that loops over left/right so I don't duplicate bone-building code, with suffix naming like "L"/"R" to keep joint and chain names unique and valid against the naming regex.

Now I'm working out the wing membrane: defining edges as paths or chains (like the arm chain itself for the leading edge, and a polyline through the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and fingertip for the trailing edge), with the bone option set to the arm chain so the membrane follows it correctly.

I'm reconsidering the full outline though — the leading edge runs shoulder-elbow-wrist-F1tip, while the outer/trailing edge should scallop across F1tip through F4tip back to the body, so I need to figure out how to split that into two root-to-tip membrane edges properly.

Pairing the leading path and a trailing path that both terminate at F1tip actually creates the right fan shape naturally, since the interior fills by matching arc-length fractions and the scallops fall out from the polyline corners. Now I'm defining the trailing path starting at a body point and running through F4tip, F3tip, F2tip to F1tip.

I'm also sketching the finger chains and membrane placement, deciding on wing mottled coloring, and planning legs with clawed feet before starting to write the actual import statements and setup code.

Now I'm setting up the foot pad geometry attached to the leg's final joint, then moving on to build the tail chain with tapering segments and a membrane connecting it to the hips.

For the tail membrane itself, I'm figuring out how to span it between the two legs and the tail — a bat's uropatagium stretches from ankle to ankle via the tail tip, so I need to connect the left leg chain, tail chain, and right leg chain with membrane geometry despite their differing start/end points.

Now I'm writing a helper to compute the midpoint between wrist and fingertip with a slight vertical offset for the finger bones.

Naming each finger chain and joint uniquely like "finger1L" and "f1L1" to avoid collisions, and the tail polyline setup looks fine. Finalizing the output now, keeping the explanation brief.
